To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stubble retention and N fertilization had a long-term impact on the size and composition of the soil microbial communities.

stubble and N addition to the soil had significant and long-term impact on the structure of the soil microbiota, and that the effects of stubble addition on soil microbial community were more significant than the N addition.
stubble retention and N application have long-term effects on soil microbial communities and the structure and functional genes of the microbial community.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of stubble management (i.e., stubble retention vs. removal) on soil microbial community and its functional gene abundance under different nitrogen application rates in a maize production systems in Australia.
understanding how agronomic management practices influence the structure of soil microbial communities and their functional genes.
the effects of stubble management on the soil microbial communities in a cropping system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stubble retention is beneficial for soil health and that stubble retention should be considered as a best practice management strategy in the Australian agricultural system.
stubble retention is the most important agronomic practice in the system for the maintenance of a healthy soil microbial community.
stubble retention is the most important factor affecting microbial community structure in the short term, while the addition of N is the most important in the longer term.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stubble retention is a more important driver than N-fertilization in regulating the microbial community and its functions.
stubble management is the primary driver in the structure of the soil microbiota and that N management has a significant impact on the functional genes involved in the C- and N-cycling processes.
stubble retention and N-fertiliser application can have significant and lasting effects on the soil microbial population, which in turn affects the soil ecosystem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stubble management and fertilizer application can have a significant impact on the structure of microbial communities.
the management of stubble and N has significant and long-term effects on soil microbial community at the phylogenetic and function levels.
the soil microbiome is a sensitive indicator of changes in soil management and can be used as a proxy for the impact of management on soil function.
